correctness.rationale: PASS: At predator-free prey equilibrium X=r/a>0 the predator linearization decouples at first order into a fixed-X renewal equation whose Euler–Lotka zero-growth mass is R_F(X). The positive baseline m ensures integrability; F(X)=O(X) at small X gives R_F→0. For δ<T, Hν(z)=∫0^z Jν(s)ds has positive slope Jν(0), so rescaling w=Xz and dominated convergence yields adult birth contribution k(F(X)/X)Aν(0)/(g Jν(0))→(kL/g)e^{-νT}; contributions over z≥δ and adult-supported basal births vanish exponentially in X. Continuity in X follows by domination. At witness T=1,ν=10,g=.01,k=3,m=.1,µM=.01,ρ=ζ=1, tildeB=(z-1)e^{-(z-1)}/100 for z≥1, survival on ages [1,2] exceeds 19/25 and adult weight ≥1/2, F(1)>99/100 for both birth laws. Hence R_F(1)>3/2*(99/100)*(19/25)=5643/5000>1. High-X limits are 300e^-10<1 and zero; low-X limit zero, giving two roots via IVT. Independently checked rational lower bound and Taylor e^10>300 and read numerical quadrature script as corroboration. No claim of exactly two crossings or nonlinear persistence.

originality.rationale: PASS (best knowledge): Original full Suarez et al. arXiv:2502.19748v1 was inspected and supplies source sigmoid age model and saturated variant (Section 7.1), but not a proof of large-prey newborn-age Laplace boundary layer nor reentrant invadability versus resource X. Resultary prior related finding studies monotonic R(g) when varying juvenile consumption g at fixed X, compatible but logically separate; and another same-model finding studies a weighted mass bound against blow-up, also separate. Classical renewal theory yields the characteristic equation but not the concrete asymptotic coefficient and simultaneous double threshold witness for both birth laws. Residual risk: model-specific asymptotics might appear elsewhere under fecundity-leakage language; no full global bibliography claim.
residual_risks: The exact high-resource limit requires fixed finite ν, positive baseline mortality, mild F growth, and adult-supported basal births; not a theorem for arbitrary age mortality.
Explicit strict R>1 at X=1 proves at least two roots, not uniqueness, transversality, or nonlinear persistence.
Model’s sigmoid permits biologically unrealistic newborn adult fecundity; the positive unsaturated high-X limit is a modeling artifact to interpret correctly.
Some older renewal modeling texts or related non-OA role-reversal papers may contain analogous boundary-layer asymptotics.

value.rationale: PASS: Exactly identifies a high-resource invasion mechanism hidden by smooth sigmoid maturation—finite positive newborn adult-birth weight yields k e^-νT/g for linear feeding even as juvenile mortality grows with X. Birth saturation removes the limit. The strict explicit two-transition example converts the boundary mechanism into a meaningful comparison of invasion regimes under both proposed birth choices, not merely a numerical parameter plot; scope appropriately limited to local invasion at predator-free equilibrium.

final_claim: For age-structured predator renewal model of Suarez et al. with finite smooth maturation, positive constant baseline mortality and eligible F(X)/X→L, R_F(0+)=0 and R_F(∞)=(kL/g)e^{-νT}. The specified positive rational example has R_F(1)>5643/5000 and at least two predator-invasion threshold crossings for both F=X and F=100tanh(X/100).
